end.summary:
Placed BCE and CE dates on a timeline in 4 of 5 unaided attempts.
Explained that BCE dates count down toward 1 BCE and CE dates move rightward.
Identified 1700 CE as part of the 18th century.
Explained why historians cross-check a ruler’s claims with other sources.
Teach-back was not passed; no misconceptions were recorded.
end.parentNote: Asha practised ordering BCE and CE dates, reading a timeline, identifying a century, and judging why historians cross-check sources. Aarav explained that 500 BCE comes before 100 CE and that a ruler’s inscription may praise the ruler, so other sources are useful. They also asked to see a drawn timeline and an inscription; using visuals at home could support this practice. The lesson did not record a misconception that needed later correction.
